title: Some in Rome even hold, with most Reformed, that it was natural as opposed to supernatural
source_text: XLIV. Imo patet ex iis quae ante retulimus, in Ecclesia Romana non deesse, qui cum plerisque Reformatis doceant justitiam Originalem pertinuisse ad dona naturae, non gratiae, prout naturae opponitur: adeoque primo homini naturalem fuisse, quatenus naturale opponitur supernaturali.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed it is clear from those things which we reported before, that in the Roman Church there are not lacking those who with most of the Reformed teach that Original justice pertained to the gifts of nature, not of grace, as it is opposed to nature: and so that it was natural to the first man, insofar as natural is opposed to supernatural.
pass_b_english: In fact, what we reported earlier shows that the Roman Church has its own teachers who side with most of the Reformed here. They hold that original righteousness was one of nature's gifts, not one of grace's, taking grace as the opposite of nature. On their view it was natural to the first man even in the sense that stands against "supernatural".

lemmas.gloss: as grace is opposed to nature

choices.english: as grace is opposed to nature
choices.why: The implied subject is gratia; the English supplies it.
